findings.text: §25 is declared `implementable`, but the plan's only open followup (`f-tsigah-repair-wave-at-95ff28824`, the last section before `</section>` at plan.html:874) recommends `/reckon-build the-suite-is-green-at-head §4`, and §4 is declared `done`; the adding commit `7567efba3` declared the section and opened no followup for it, so nothing in the plan invokes §25

findings.reason: a node adopting the supplied reason writes a whitelist comment that does not cover the flagged operation, instead of establishing the exemption the section asks for and stopping blocked with the change if the owner can serve it.
findings.text: §25 asks whether `_bound_server_log`'s publish of the predecessor is an exception "the owner cannot serve" and then supplies the reason "The live file is emptied in place because the server unit holds it open for appending", but the operation the census flags is the other one: `_staged_writes` reports a locally staged rename source, and I confirmed on a synthetic tree that the `staging = predecessor.with_name(predecessor.name + ".tmp"); shutil.copyfile(target, staging); os.replace(staging, predecessor)` sequence is reported while a bare `with target.open("wb"): pass` is not; `write_atomically` publishes a single file through exactly a sibling temporary renamed into place, so the append-mode fact explains the in-place truncation (which is not a staged write) and does not establish that the owner cannot serve the flagged predecessor publish
